title: Review: the sixteen software interface specifications, their source fidelity at the pinned commit and the honesty of their interface-level gap lists
lifecycle_status_note: 'draft' rather than 'reviewed' or 'approved': this record is the output of an automated review pass and no human reviewer has confirmed it. automated_review_status below refers to corpus automation only and is not a statement about engineering validity.

revision_history.author: sw_engineer
revision_history.description: First issue. Domain review of all sixteen software_interface_specification records, FB2-SW-IFS-000001 through FB2-SW-IFS-000016. Every one of the sixteen was read and every source citation it makes was checked against the pinned foxBMS commit by reading the blob, not the working tree. The review covers five things: source grounding, hash and line-range fidelity, honesty of the anti-conformance fields, oracle basis and execution classification, and profile discipline. Measured results: 81 of 81 declared source_refs resolve to real entries in docs/artifacts/sources/source-registry.json; 61 of 61 element declaration_line values land on a line that carries the claimed symbol at commit 308028fb; 60 of 61 element implementation_line values do likewise, the single exception being FB2-REV-FND-000193; 572 of 572 in-record 'path Lnn-Lmm' prose ranges resolve inside the file they name and are within its bounds; 70 of 70 interface_level_gaps evidence ranges likewise; all sixteen records carry a populated not_specified_by_source list (57 lists, 194 entries) and a non-empty interface_level_gaps list (48 gaps in total); all sixteen carry verification_status with analysed_against_running_code false and conformance_tested false, and not one claims verification; all sixteen declare human_approval_status 'pending', production_authorized false and product_verification_credit false; no ISO 26262 conformity, certification, tool-qualification or ASPICE capability-level claim was found in any of the sixteen, and no standards_mappings entry claims the stronger status 'mapped'. Four findings are recorded. Nothing in this review asserts that the sixteen interfaces are correctly specified; it asserts only what was measured, and the measurement is of provenance fidelity, not of interface correctness.

reviewer_identity.note: Automated review performed in a single AI coding-agent session (opencode). The model identifier is the identifier exposed to this session's runtime. No platform-issued session id was available to the reviewer, so session_id is a locally chosen label for this run and is not a platform-issued identifier. Per master-prompt clause 2.9 this is an automated review: it is NOT organizational independence, NOT human confirmation, and NOT a qualified-checker result. No human reviewer, independent party, or separate agent session participated. Each of the sixteen records already states this of itself in analysis.independence = 'not_independent'; this review does not improve on that and does not claim to.

scope: Full scope over all sixteen software_interface_specification records in the corpus: FB2-SW-IFS-000001 through FB2-SW-IFS-000016, every one at revision 1. All sixteen declare profile 'synthetic_reference' and there is no as_is software_interface_specification record in this corpus, so this single profile-scoped review covers every record of the type and no reviewed_id below resolves ambiguously. FB2-REV-FND-000046 records why that matters: a profile-scoped review cannot cover both profiles' records under a shared identifier, because doing so would assert that one review examined two different records that share a string. It is checked here rather than assumed - see review_method.per_profile_check. Each record's full text was read, and every source citation it makes was checked by reading the blob at commit 308028fb rather than the working tree, because the records' own method is 'source_analysis_at_pinned_commit' and verifying that claim against the working tree would not verify it. NOT IN SCOPE: whether the sixteen interfaces are correctly specified, whether the described behaviour is the behaviour the product should have, whether the consuming modules named exist with the responsibilities attributed to them, and the assembler routine behind FAS_DisableInterrupts, which is outside the C language boundary these records declare.

findings.description: The FAS_DisableInterrupts element records its implementation as src/app/main/include/fassert.h line 112. That line does not carry the pragma, the declaration, or any code: it is a continuation line of the doxygen comment above the declaration, reading '*          by writing to the SPSR (Saved Program Status Register) register'. The supervisor-call pragma the element is actually bound by, '#pragma SWI_ALIAS(FAS_DisableInterrupts, 5)', is at line 116, and the declaration 'extern void FAS_DisableInterrupts(void);' is at line 117. The reference is therefore off by four lines and lands on prose inside a comment. This is one wrong structured line reference out of the sixty-one implementation_line values across the sixteen records, and the other sixty are exact; it is recorded as a real defect rather than dismissed as noise because a structured field is the one a machine reads. The same record carries four prose references to 'the pragma ... at src/app/main/include/fassert.h L112', in validity_signalling.evidence, concurrency.protection_mechanism evidence, the gap evidence for the depth-counter gap, and the element's own summary evidence. All four name the same wrong line.
findings.evidence: Read from the blob at commit 308028fb, not the working tree. src/app/main/include/fassert.h lines 109-117: 109 '/**', 110 ' * @brief   Disable interrupts', 111 ' * @details This alias is mapped to an ASM function and disables all interrupts', 112 ' *          by writing to the SPSR (Saved Program Status Register) register', 113 ' *          through the control field mask byte PSR[7:0] (privileged', 114 ' *          software execution)', 115 ' */', 116 '#pragma SWI_ALIAS(FAS_DisableInterrupts, 5)', 117 'extern void FAS_DisableInterrupts(void);'. The record's declaration_line of 117 is CORRECT and its declaration symbol check passes; only implementation_line is wrong. Method: for each of the sixteen records, each element's declared symbol was searched for on the declared implementation line in the blob at the pinned commit. 60 of 61 matched, 1 did not, and that one is this element.

findings.description: The same record is internally inconsistent about where the pragma is, in a way no single line-reference check would catch. One sentence says the pragma is 'on the line above it' - immediately above the declaration at line 117 - and in the same sentence says it is 'at src/app/main/include/fassert.h L112'. Those cannot both be true: 112 is five lines above 117 and four lines above the pragma at 116. The record therefore asserts a relative position and an absolute position for the same construct, and the absolute one is wrong. This is recorded separately from FB2-REV-FND-000193 because fixing the line number alone does not fix it - a reader who corrects 112 to 116 still has to notice that the sentence's two claims now agree, and one who does not will re-derive the wrong line from the relative claim. No conclusion of the record depends on which line the pragma is on; the binding relationship it asserts is real and is at 116.
findings.evidence: validity_signalling.evidence of the FAS_DisableInterrupts element, quoted from the record: 'The element has no C implementation at all: it is bound to an assembler routine by the supervisor-call pragma on the line above it, #pragma SWI_ALIAS(FAS_DisableInterrupts, 5) at src/app/main/include/fassert.h L112'. Cross-checked against the blob at 308028fb: pragma at 116, declaration at 117, so 'the line above it' is correct and 'L112' is not.

findings.description: The record's provenance is thinner than its own method claims in one specific place, and this is the finding the review was looking for. Every element in all sixteen records is grounded in a file:line citation that this review verified. The FAS_DisableInterrupts element is the one element in the family whose behaviour is NOT in a C file the record can cite, because it is an assembler routine reached through a supervisor-call alias. The record is honest that it cannot analyse the routine - it says so in interface_level_gaps and in what_this_record_is_not - but it grounds that admission in the source's own doc comment, which names the routine's location as 'src\os\freertos\portable\ccs\arm_cortex-r5\portasm.asm'. That path does not exist at commit 308028fb. The file that does exist is src/os/freertos/freertos/portable/ccs/arm_cortex-r5/portasm.asm, which has an extra 'freertos' path segment; and the routine is in fact locatable in it, swiPortDisableInterrupts at line 313, dispatched from the SWI vector table at line 307. So the record's statement that the source 'names as being in the RTOS port' is true but weaker than the truth available, and its method claim - source_analysis_at_pinned_commit, tools_used including 'git show 308028fb:<path>' - was not carried through to the one claim in the family that rests on a path the commit does not contain. The record does not assert the routine was located, so this is not a false statement; it is a citation the method did not verify, and the review verified it and found the named path stale.
findings.evidence: The doc comment at src/app/main/include/fassert.h lines 105-108 at commit 308028fb names 'src\os\freertos\portable\ccs\arm_cortex-r5\portasm.asm::swiPortDisableInterrupts' with backslash separators. 'git ls-tree -r --name-only 308028fb' lists exactly one portasm file: src/os/freertos/freertos/portable/ccs/arm_cortex-r5/portasm.asm. Reading it: line 307 '.word   swiPortDisableInterrupts ; 5 - vPortDisableInterrupts' and line 313 'swiPortDisableInterrupts'. The SWI number 5 in '#pragma SWI_ALIAS(FAS_DisableInterrupts, 5)' matches the dispatch comment on line 307, which corroborates that the routine the record declines to analyse is the one the pragma names. The record's own text, quoted: 'FAS_DisableInterrupts is declared at src/app/main/include/fassert.h L117 and bound by the pragma on L112 to an assembler routine the source names as being in the RTOS port.'

findings.description: This record names FB2-SW-DSN-000002 in prose without a profile qualifier, and that identifier is one of the thirty-nine carried by two live records, one per profile. Under ID-RULE-004 as amended on 2026-10-04 this is CONFORMANT and is not a violation: the sharing is permitted, and this finding is not a cross-profile collision finding. What is reported is reference ambiguity, and it is the only one of the sixteen records that exhibits it. The corpus convention resolves the reference to the synthetic_reference copy, and because this record is itself synthetic_reference the convention and the enclosing profile agree, so on the evidence there is no wrong answer here. It is recorded because the condition is real and machine-visible, because the corpus now has a detector for it, and because a reader auditing this record should know that one of its cross-references depends on a convention rather than on a field. corpus.py reports this class under rule unqualified_reference_ambiguity, severity medium, report-only and not gated. The remaining fifteen records were checked for the same condition and name no shared identifier at all.
findings.evidence: FB2-SW-IFS-000011 (docs/artifacts/corpus/synthetic_reference/software/ifs-redundancy-mrc.json) contains the string FB2-SW-DSN-000002 outside any profile-qualified slot. FB2-SW-DSN-000002 is carried by two live records: docs/artifacts/corpus/as_is/software/design-soa.json and docs/artifacts/corpus/synthetic_reference/software/design-soa.json. Sweep of all sixteen records for shared identifiers: FB2-SW-IFS-000011 is the only hit; the other fifteen name none of the thirty-nine.

dispositions.action: Accepted as a real provenance defect in one record. NOT repaired by this review. Correcting implementation_line and the four prose references is an edit to a record's engineering content, and a review is not the instrument that makes such an edit: the repair belongs to the record's owner, who must decide whether the field should name the pragma at 116, the declaration at 117, or be dropped, because 'implementation' is not a well-defined concept for an element that has no C implementation - which is itself part of what this record gets right by saying so in its gaps. Left standing as a finding. No finding was weakened and no record was edited to make this disappear.

Accepted. Same reasoning as FB2-REV-FND-000193: recorded, not repaired, because the repair requires the record owner's judgement about which of the sentence's two claims survives. The finding names both claims so that whoever repairs it does not have to re-derive the contradiction.

Accepted, and referred to the record owner as an open provenance question rather than a defect. The record makes no false statement, so there is nothing to correct; what is missing is a recorded discrepancy between the path in the source's doc comment and the path in the tree at the pinned commit. Deciding whether to record that discrepancy, and whether to extend the specification across the language boundary into the assembler routine, is a scope decision for the interface owner and not a reviewer's. This review supplies the measurement - the named path does not resolve, the real path does, and the routine is at line 313 of it - so the decision can be taken against evidence rather than re-derived.

Accepted and carried forward. It is conformant under amended ID-RULE-004 and is explicitly not treated as a violation. No reference was rewritten: qualifying it would be a text edit to a record's content, and under the amended rule no qualification is required. The finding is recorded so that the one cross-reference in this family which rests on the corpus convention rather than on a field is visible to a reader, and so that this review's own coverage claim can be checked.

limitations: Automated AI review performed in a single agent session. It is not organizational independence, not human confirmation, and not a qualified-checker result (master-prompt clause 2.9). Every one of the sixteen records declares independence 'not_independent' about itself; this review does not improve on that and does not claim to.
human_approval_status is 'pending' for all sixteen records and for this review. No human reviewer signed any of them.

No artifact covered by this review carries production authority or product verification credit. All sixteen declare production_authorized false and product_verification_credit false, and this review asserts neither.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY VERIFIED, and how: (a) every declared source_refs entry was resolved against docs/artifacts/sources/source-registry.json - 81 of 81 resolve, 0 dangling; (b) for every element of every record, the declared symbol was searched for on the declared declaration_line and implementation_line in the blob at commit 308028fb, read with git show so that the working tree was never consulted - 61 of 61 declaration lines carry the claimed symbol, 60 of 61 implementation lines do; (c) every 'path Lnn' and 'path Lnn-Lmm' citation appearing anywhere in the sixteen records was resolved in the blob at the same commit and range-checked against the file's real length - 572 of 572 in bounds, 0 outside, 0 unparseable, 0 naming a file absent from the commit; (d) the same check applied to interface_level_gaps evidence alone: 70 of 70 in bounds; (e) the anti-conformance fields were read field by field on all sixteen; (f) a pattern search for conformity, certification, capability-level, qualified-checker and organizational-independence language was run over the serialized text of all sixteen and every hit was read in context - 0 unnegated claims; (g) every standards_mappings entry was read for status - 0 of 30 entries claim 'mapped', all are 'partially_mapped'; (h) the oracle and execution fields were read on all sixteen.

WHAT WAS NOT VERIFIED, and this is the larger half: whether any of the sixteen interfaces is correctly specified. A source citation can be exact and the specification built on it can still be wrong - a misread control flow, a wrong caller, a mis-stated consequence. This review checked that the records point at the source accurately; it did not check that their reading of the source is right. No C file was analysed for behaviour beyond confirming that a named symbol occurs on a named line, so a claim of the form 'the timer guard returns at L286' was checked for line existence and not for whether line 286 is the timer guard.

No C file was compiled, linked or executed. No test was run against any of these interfaces. Nothing here is evidence that any interface behaves as described at run time, and the records themselves say so: all sixteen declare verification_status with analysed_against_running_code false and conformance_tested false, and not one of the sixteen claims verification of any kind.

The consuming modules named by the sixteen records were NOT checked to exist, and no interface agreement was checked for. A consuming module named in consumption_evidence was accepted as named. This is a real gap in the review's coverage and is stated rather than left implicit.

The assembler routine behind FAS_DisableInterrupts was located for the purposes of FB2-REV-FND-000195 and its dispatch was read, but its body was NOT analysed and no claim is made about what it does. The sixteen records place it outside their declared boundary and this review does not cross that boundary.

The sixteen records' own interface_level_gaps were checked for structure and for citation resolvability only. Whether each gap is the RIGHT gap - whether a more consequential interface-level problem was missed - is a completeness judgement that this review does not make and does not claim.

The single wrong line reference found (FB2-REV-FND-000193) was found by exhaustive automated checking of all 61 implementation lines and all 572 prose ranges. The check is sound for the class 'does this line exist, is it in bounds, does it carry this symbol'. It cannot detect a citation that is in bounds and carries the right symbol but attributes the wrong significance to it. A residue of semantically-wrong-but-positionally-correct citations is therefore not excluded, and quantifying it would require reading each of the sixteen against its source in full, which is a re-authoring exercise rather than a review.

The 16 parameters carrying neither valid_range nor range_evidence were examined and are NOT a finding. Each is the placeholder entry for a zero-parameter function, named '(none)', emitted so that the parameters array is never empty; there is no parameter for a range to describe. Recorded here so that a reader who runs the same mechanical check does not report it as a defect.
review_method: Direct source verification against the pinned commit, not against the working tree. Every one of the sixteen records declares analysis.method 'source_analysis_at_pinned_commit' and names commit 308028fb; eight name it in short form and eight name the full 40-character SHA, which resolve to the same commit (verified: git rev-parse 308028fb equals 308028fb13d046ba29b98886895c2e17937b1437), so the two forms are treated as one pin and the mixed precision is noted in results_summary rather than raised as a finding. Every file the records cite was read with 'git show 308028fb:<path>' so that the claim being verified is the claim about the pinned blob. Four checks were run mechanically and their results are counted in results_summary: source_refs resolution against the source registry; element declaration_line and implementation_line symbol presence; every 'path Lnn[-Lmm]' citation in the whole serialized record, resolved and range-checked; and the same over interface_level_gaps evidence alone. Two checks were run by reading: the anti-conformance fields field by field, and a pattern search for conformity, certification, capability-level, qualified-checker and independence language, every hit of which was read in context before being counted. One check was run as a counterfactual on the profile question: per_profile_check. All sixteen records declare profile 'synthetic_reference' and the corpus contains no as_is software_interface_specification record, which was established by enumeration rather than assumed, so the FB2-REV-FND-000046 prohibition on a profile-scoped review spanning two profiles' records under a shared identifier cannot arise here and one review is the correct number. FINDINGS WERE SOUGHT, NOT CONFIRMED: the line-fidelity check was expected to be clean because the same family passed it elsewhere, and it did not, and the one failure was investigated to its cause rather than being recorded and dropped.

results_summary.per_profile_check: all sixteen declare profile 'synthetic_reference'; enumeration of the corpus finds no as_is software_interface_specification record, so one profile-scoped review covers the whole family and FB2-REV-FND-000046 does not arise. ESTABLISHED BY ENUMERATION, not assumed.
results_summary.pin_precision_observation: eight records pin commit 308028fb in short form and eight pin the full 40-character SHA; both resolve to 308028fb13d046ba29b98886895c2e17937b1437, so the pin is unambiguous in all sixteen. Recorded as an observation in results_summary and not raised as a finding, because it changes no citation and resolves to the same commit.
results_summary.parameters_without_valid_range_dispositi: examined and NOT a finding: all sixteen are the '(none)' placeholder emitted for a zero-parameter function, so there is no parameter for a range to describe. Recorded so a reader repeating the check does not report it.
